claims.text: A friend who received a reply from one of the owner's agents said on WhatsApp that the amount of text he produces is baffling, and the honest answer deserved numbers.
claims.quote: the amount of text I manage to produce is baffling

claims.text: In twenty-seven days the owner sent 148 messages, 65,323 words in all, of which 55,473 were in thirty-seven long voice memos.
claims.quote: In twenty-seven days I sent 148 messages, 65,323 words in all, of which 55,473 were in thirty-seven long voice memos

value.unit: words sent by the owner in 27 days

claims.text: The agent published twenty-two articles totalling 96,451 words with 105 figures and wrote 75,993 words to the owner about them.
claims.quote: The agent published twenty-two articles totalling 96,451 words with 105 figures, wrote 75,993 words to me about them

claims.text: The site went through 123 releases in the window, each with a version number, a log entry and a commit carrying both names.
claims.quote: and made 123 releases of the site

claims.text: To do it the agent ran 135 web searches, 190 page fetches, 2,001 shell commands and 26 research agents.
claims.quote: It ran 135 web searches, 190 page fetches, 2,001 shell commands and 26 research agents to do it.

claims.text: No article came from a one-line prompt: the shortest brief was one memo of 1,943 words with nothing after it, the longest ran to twenty-one messages.
claims.quote: The shortest brief any article had was one memo of 1,943 words with nothing after it

claims.text: The median message is sixty-seven words; thirty-seven messages over four hundred words carry 85% of the total and are the voice memos.
claims.quote: the median message is sixty-seven words long

claims.text: Of the 148 messages, forty-six are corrections, five plain approvals, and fifty-two open with an approving word and then ask for something.
claims.quote: Of the 148, forty-six are corrections and five are plain approvals

claims.text: The fractal semantic graphs article took 2,395 words from the owner in twenty-one turns and came out at 2,447 words over five releases, argued down to the right ones.
claims.quote: 2,395 words from me, 2,447 words out, five releases

value.unit: words of input to the fractal semantic graphs article

claims.text: Corrections arrive within the hour and are carried in minutes: a median of thirty-eight minutes from a release to the next correction, and five minutes to the release that carries it.
claims.quote: a median of thirty-eight minutes from a release to my next correction, and five minutes from the correction to the release that carries it

value.unit: minutes, median, from release to correction

claims.text: The corrections were rarely to hallucinations; they were to briefs that needed to be better: direction, framing, voice, vocabulary and scope.
claims.quote: I said in the memo that these days I rarely experience hallucinations; I experience briefs that need to be better

claims.text: The clearest direction correction: a folder tree is not a fractal semantic graph, because zooming into a node puts you in a different universe with its own vocabulary.
claims.quote: zooming into a node of a fractal semantic graph puts you in a different universe with its own vocabulary

claims.text: One word for a step of a ladder, found twenty-eight times in one article, was banned from every article the way the em-dash was, with a check in the build.
claims.quote: asked for it to go the way of the em-dash, which it did, from every article, with a check in the build so it cannot come back

claims.text: A model that can write well in every direction needs a person with a direction, and every correction narrows the space for the next one.
claims.quote: A model that can write well in every direction needs a person with a direction

claims.text: The code review company article quotes or links thirty-three pieces of the owner's earlier writing, none written for the article.
claims.quote: The code review company article quotes or links thirty-three pieces of my earlier writing.

value.unit: pieces of earlier writing quoted or linked

claims.text: The record behind it: the O2 Platform from 2010, a 2016 book, 107 posts on diniscruz.ai in twenty months, 3,025 markdown files in one team's record, and the twenty-six earlier articles.
claims.quote: 107 posts on diniscruz.ai between February 2024 and October 2025

value.unit: posts on diniscruz.ai in twenty months

claims.text: The agent is fast because the record exists and is published where a machine can read it; without it the same memo would produce a plausible essay with nothing under it.
claims.quote: The agent is fast because the record exists and is published where a machine can read it

claims.text: The ideas moved in a Wardley-evolution way from genesis, a tool and a blog post, through custom-built, a book and talks, to something like a product an agent can be pointed at.
claims.quote: The ideas moved from genesis, a tool and a blog post, through custom-built, a book and talks, to something like a product

claims.text: The production pipeline, memo to markdown to figures to graph JSON to build, validator, leak scan and live check, is as much the input as the memos, and all of it is open source.
claims.quote: The whole of that is open source, in the site's own repository.

claims.text: The tools inside the pipeline were almost all built on the day they were needed because something was slow; the transcript parser was about forty lines.
claims.quote: The tools inside it were almost all built on the day they were needed, because something was slow.

claims.text: The productivity is not the model but the model inside a form the owner controls, where any step that is not working is replaced with a tool the same day.
claims.quote: The productivity is not the model. It is the model inside a form I control

claims.text: Everything measured is a file in the evidence vault: 266 rows of the session record, 124 releases, per-article ledgers, twenty-eight corrections with their latency, seventy-five saved versions.
claims.quote: the twenty-eight corrections with how long each waited

value.unit: corrections in the vault with their latency

claims.text: The vault corrected the article twice, a double-counted compaction count and a message count including client rows, and both corrections are left visible.
claims.quote: The vault also corrected this article, twice, and I have left both corrections visible rather than silently fixing the numbers

claims.text: The published trail of an idea, with its graphs and corrections, is a better thing for a model to learn from than anything it can find on its own.
claims.quote: The trail is a better thing for a model to learn from than anything it can find on its own.

claims.text: Seventeen of the twenty-seven earlier articles cite at least one earlier one, sixty-five links run between them, and six run the other way from an updated older article.
claims.quote: Seventeen of the twenty-seven articles before this one cite at least one earlier one, sixty-five links run between them

claims.text: Eleven times in the session the context was compacted, and on nine of those days the work carried on with releases the same day, because the record was good enough to rebuild from.
claims.quote: Eleven times in the session the context was compacted

claims.text: People who see the output and say they are out of a job have the arrow wrong: the person with the direction, the taste and the twenty years is what the agent is for.
claims.quote: They are more relevant, not less. They are the input.

claims.text: The attribution of input to article is hand-checked for eight articles and a stated heuristic for the rest, with the message ids on record.
claims.quote: The attribution of input to article is hand-checked for eight articles and a stated heuristic for the rest

claims.text: The 2010 to 2016 record is quoted but not counted, and the diniscruz.ai count is of posts, not words.
claims.quote: The 2010 to 2016 record is quoted from but not counted; the diniscruz.ai count is of posts, not words.

claims.text: The biggest input of all, the conversations and the work the memos came out of, is in no record and never will be.
claims.quote: the conversations and the work the memos came out of, is not in any record and never will be

claims.text: The transcript begins on 9 September, so the first seven articles, written in August, are not in it.
claims.quote: The transcript file begins on 9 September, so the first seven articles on this site, written in August, are not in it.

claims.text: ChatGPT's one-page infographic, second version, was checked against the article; its headline figures are right and two numbers are wrong, named in the caption.
claims.quote: Two numbers are not: the input for the code review company article is given as 5,785 words

claims.text: The data is the transcript of the Claude Code session that has run the site since 11 August, parsed for who said what and when, joined to the site's git history.
claims.quote: The data is the transcript of the Claude Code session that has run this site since 11 August
